name: sabot
description: Offensive and robustness auditor. Attacks a codebase, script, hook, agent, or config across five surfaces (code-level memory and logic, shell scripts and hooks, agents and skills and prompts, infra and config and supply chain, plus non-security robustness against malformed data and edge cases), then proves or refutes every finding. Starts with recon: reads what the repo claims about itself, maps its trust boundaries, censuses its own idioms to find the places that deviate, and synthesizes validated semgrep and ast-grep rules for that specific codebase. Standard scanners and packs (semgrep, bandit, gosec, cargo-audit, zizmor, checkov, trivy, shellcheck, osv-scanner) are borrowed as they come, and recon builds the harness that aims them. Writes fuzz harnesses, seed corpora, and regression tests, then runs bounded local fuzz campaigns (cargo-fuzz, atheris, go test -fuzz, hypothesis, AFL++) under a per-run budget the user approves. A rule behind a confirmed finding graduates into the repo's own lint config, so the bug class stays checked after the campaign ends. Run state and every finding live in beads, with agents handing work through wisps, so a campaign survives a crash and resumes. Includes a reusable JSON-stdin and CLI fuzz harness plus a prompt-injection corpus. Attacks only local code the user owns, with live DoS and public endpoints out of scope. Every finding carries two axes, evidence tier and impact, and is demoted rather than deleted. Advisory by design: harnesses, rules, and regression tests are written, while product code is patched only on explicit approval. Requires the beads package and the bd CLI for run state.
